findings.title: Rendering a relationship-selected XML part can bypass the depth limit and abort the host
findings.summary: A document can place deeply nested numbering XML in a .bin part and reference it with the numbering relationship. Admission skips its XML policy; rendering later passes it to the recursive unchecked DOM parser, allowing a small input to overflow the host stack.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled document bytes reach unbounded recursion through an ordinary conversion API. Process availability impact is medium and likelihood is high once the document is converted; no remote deployment is assumed.

confidence.rationale: Static trace establishes suffix-based admission, arbitrary relationship target selection, and recursive parsing without a depth guard. No crash input was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Admission checks XML by filename suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: An auxiliary .bin part is only drained and charged to the inflation budget; its XML depth and tag policy are never inspected.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship type selects an arbitrary part name
codeEvidence.explanation: A numbering relationship may point to a non-.xml internal part; no suffix or content-policy check is applied here.

codeEvidence.label: Numbering loader invokes unchecked DOM parser
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected part bytes become a string and enter Dom::parse_xdocument regardless of their filename.

codeEvidence.label: Unchecked parser recurses for each nested element
codeEvidence.explanation: Each nested '<' adds another parse_element stack frame without checking InputLimits.

rootCause.summary: admit classifies auxiliary XML by filename suffix, while main_rel_part classifies it by relationship type. load_numbering bridges those inconsistent classifications and sends the unvalidated bytes to parse_xdocument, whose parse_element calls itself for every nested element. The main-part fallback check does not protect auxiliary numbering parts.

findings.remediation: Apply the active XML depth/tag policy to every relationship-selected XML consumer before constructing its DOM, or classify all XML content types during admission and retain checked depth at each unchecked consumer.

limitations: No runtime crash reproduction; affected thread stack size and host isolation determine failure threshold.
validation.summary: with_layout admits input at src/convert/mod.rs:776, then opens the same package and reaches collect_blocks at :923. collect_blocks calls load_numbering at :7734. A valid internal numbering relationship to a .bin part passes admission's byte limits and main-part check yet reaches unchecked recursive parsing. strict_to_transitional_docx_within only rewrites .xml/.rels names (:810) and PartFs read_package only applies metadata checks to [Content_Types].xml/.rels (:354). Neither inserts the missing depth check.
counterevidence: Ordinary .xml/.rels parts are depth-checked; the main document is explicitly checked even with a different extension.
ZIP entry/part/total byte limits and process limits reduce blast radius but do not bound recursive depth of this auxiliary part.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> admit suffix filter -> internal numbering relationship -> part_string -> parse_numbering_xml -> recursive parse_element
dataflow.source: Attacker-controlled auxiliary package part and relationship
dataflow.outcome: Stack exhaustion terminates the processing thread/process, including an embedding Python host.

impact.why: Availability loss of the process converting the document.

likelihood.why: The attacker chooses both relationship target and deeply nested part bytes; current parser has no guard.

reachability.summary: An untrusted-document supplier needs the victim to call a normal PDF/PNG/render-report conversion; no filesystem or configuration privileges are required.
preconditions: Victim converts the supplied package; it contains valid root metadata and main document.

attackPath.summary: Supply an otherwise valid DOCX with an internal numbering relationship targeting word/numbering.bin containing deeply nested XML; ask the library or CLI to render it.

remediationTests: Verify that rendering refuses a numbering relationship targeting deeply nested .bin XML with INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Apply the same regression to renamed styles, headers, footers, notes, settings and other relationship-selected XML parts.

findings.title: Permitted pull requests execute code on shared self-hosted infrastructure
findings.summary: Pull-request jobs execute the PR checkout, including a mutable local action and Cargo code, on self-hosted runners used by trusted branch jobs. The committed action describes a shared persistent checkout/store and tokenless private-network cache; permitting an attacker PR run grants runner filesystem and network authority.

severity.rationale: Impact can be high for the runner account and private build infrastructure, but likelihood depends on fork-run approval and runner-group/isolation settings unavailable offline. The source does not establish access to release credentials.

confidence.rationale: PR trigger, self-hosted execution and local checkout execution are explicit. Shared private cache/persistence are documented in the committed action; live isolation and approval policy were not inspected.

codeEvidence.label: Pull requests trigger the shared CI workflow
codeEvidence.explanation: No trusted-ref or fork condition restricts this trigger.

codeEvidence.label: PR checkout runs on self-hosted infrastructure
codeEvidence.code:
lint:
    name: fmt + clippy
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@89b12181fb390509a0842a86cc55eeb8eb928c1d # stable branch, pinned 2026-10-01
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
          # jubarte-wasm is linted for the target it ships on.
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
      - uses: ./.github/actions/mbx
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
codeEvidence.explanation: Checkout selects the PR merge tree; the local action and Cargo build execute attacker-editable code with runner authority.

codeEvidence.label: Cache endpoint is shared and unauthenticated by design
codeEvidence.code:
# The self-hosted runners share one mbx cache server on their private Docker
# network (`mbx-cache`), so a crate one runner compiled is a cache hit on the
# others. The server takes no token: mbx sends none over plain HTTP, and only
# the runners can reach it. mbx publishes only from pushes to a protected
# branch; pull requests read. GitHub-hosted runners cannot reach the server,
# so jobs that also run there keep Swatinem/rust-cache on those legs.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: jdx/mr-boxington-action@47ce49b32025d93a7a2f4570815afaa2b7092240 # v1.7.2
      with:
        backend: remote
        version: "1.24.1"
        remote-url: http://mbx-cache:7543
        namespace: jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines
codeEvidence.explanation: Committed topology describes private-network access from runners and configures the cache consumer's concrete HTTP endpoint.

codeEvidence.label: Runner checkout and store are reused
codeEvidence.code:
# Every job on a runner builds in the same checkout, so mbx always counts
    # that checkout's managed target as the most recently used and never
    # collects it: on 2026-10-17 three of them reached 69-220 GiB in a few
    # hours and filled the disk the four runners share. Each job now starts
    # from an empty target, restored from the store and the cache server,
    # and each runner's store keeps to a fixed share of the disk.
codeEvidence.explanation: The documented shared writable resources bridge PR execution and later jobs.

rootCause.summary: The workflow assigns unreviewed PR source to the same self-hosted execution class used for main and executes a repository-local composite action. Read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and disabled checkout credential persistence do not sandbox those commands. The private-cache reader convention is client-side and cannot restrain arbitrary commands supplied by the PR.

findings.remediation: Move every untrusted PR job to hosted or disposable isolated runners without private trusted-network access or shared writable state. Enforce trusted-ref restrictions for persistent runner groups and expose only a separately isolated server-enforced read-only cache to PR jobs.

limitations: No workflow was run and no host/network endpoint contacted.
validation.summary: Validated the unrestricted pull_request trigger and self-hosted lint/test/coverage jobs in ci.yml and corresponding docs, md-roundtrip and adoption jobs. The local mbx action can itself be changed by a PR. Its consumers use http://mbx-cache:7543 and reusable local state. No per-PR execution isolation is defined in this repository.
counterevidence: Some fork runs may require GitHub approval; exploitation requires a permitted run.
Workflow contents permission is read-only and checkout does not retain credentials.
Runner deployment and cache server implementation are external; credential access or successful cache poisoning was not demonstrated.

dataflow.summary: PR checkout -> local action/Cargo invocation -> self-hosted runner process -> runner files/private network
dataflow.outcome: Execution with infrastructure authority beyond submitting source.

impact.why: Arbitrary commands can access the runner account and private build infrastructure.

likelihood.why: Approval and runner isolation prerequisites are external and unknown.

reachability.summary: Requires a PR run permitted by repository approval and runner access policy. Persistence/network exposure follows the committed topology; stronger external isolation would reduce impact.

attackPath.summary: Author a PR changing a local action or Cargo build script; once its run is permitted, the self-hosted job executes it with runner authority.

remediationTests: Assert fork/untrusted PR workflows cannot select persistent trusted runners.
Verify PR worker disposal and separation from main/release writable state and private cache administration.

originalCandidate.originalReport: Public-repo pull_request CI executes attacker-controlled checkout on self-hosted runner without fork/trust gate. .github/workflows/ci.yml:16,36-49; docs.yml PR trigger+self-hosted+run scripts/gen_docs.sh; md-roundtrip/adoption same. .github/actions/mbx/action.yml says runners share private Docker network, tokenless HTTP mbx-cache:7543, and same checkout/store. Fork PR can change build.rs/local action/tests/scripts to execute runner commands when GitHub permits the run, reach private network/poison persistent host for protected jobs. persist-credentials:false/read-only token do not constrain host execution.

fullResult.title: Untrusted pull requests execute on persistent self-hosted runners
fullResult.attacker: Fork PR author whose run is permitted by GitHub repository-level approval settings
fullResult.impact: Runner-account execution, private Docker network access, possible interference with later jobs. Credential theft/protected-build compromise not established offline.
counterevidence: contents:read and persist-credentials:false restrict workflow token only
No live runner inspection; persistence/network facts from committed action
fullResult.remediation: Isolate untrusted jobs on ephemeral runners without trusted network/shared state; server-enforced read-only cache.

candidate.title: Unbounded HTML colspan expansion during altChunk conversion

A tiny admitted HTML altChunk can demand billions of generated XML elements before layout; no HTML-derived output/column budget.

candidate.originalReport: WMF EXTTEXTOUT validates record size/advance but takes n-byte text from entire file at data.get(at..at+n), not current record (src/convert/metafile.rs:603-611), then copies into retained MetaText. Repeated 14-byte records can each claim 65535 bytes overlapping subsequent records; approximately 1 MiB -> 4GiB retained text. Polygon/polyline siblings may share boundary error. Needs record-scoped slicing and budget.
